problem: Criminal penalties were not reducing harm.
title: Portugal decriminalises personal drug possession and shifts to treatment
context: Portugal faced high rates of problem drug use and HIV among people who inject drugs.
decision_made: Treat possession of small amounts for personal use as an administrative matter and expand treatment and health services.
observed_outcome: Reports describe falls in drug-related deaths and new HIV diagnoses, and no clear rise in drug use. Some trends reversed after 2011, and the effect on drug use remains debated.
lessons: Reform paired with treatment funding may reduce harms, but benefits can depend on continued investment.
limitations: Figures differ by source, definition and year. Much of the data comes from advocacy briefs and summaries. A global decline in cannabis use confounds drug-use trends.

claims.claim_text: Portugal decriminalised personal drug possession in 2001 and expanded treatment.
Reports describe drug-related deaths and HIV diagnoses falling after the reform, with debate over drug use levels.
